headline: Still no run since the trail block — the pause has clearly crossed from absorption into an open-ended gap. Steps stay high as the only load. The first structured session is now overdue as data.
confidence_reasons: Limited data sources active in last 3 days

sections.overview: The picture is unchanged in shape but longer in duration: running is fully paused, strength hasn't reappeared either, and the only thing carrying load is a persistently high step count that has held steady across the entire break. That step floor is real background work — enough to keep the athlete moving daily — but it isn't structured stimulus in any zone that develops the qualities this athlete trains for. The recent four-week running total still towers over the prior block because of the trail week, so the volume context reads as a build even though nothing has been logged for days. Recovery signals are mixed and quiet: the strain reading has fallen to nothing while tolerance sits on a month of accumulated load, which is exactly what a genuine layoff looks like on paper rather than a red flag on its own. The core tension now is that everything structured — run and strength alike — remains switched off together.
sections.trends: The 16-week shape is a clear ramp into the trail block followed by a flat line, and the year-to-date comparison against last year remains enormous — this year's accumulated distance dwarfs the same point in 2025. That long-term base is intact and isn't going anywhere on this timescale. What's worth naming is that the current flat stretch has now run long enough that it reads less like the tail of a big block and more like an unplanned trough. For an athlete building year-round durable capacity rather than periodising to an event, a trough this long without a re-entry point starts to work against the consistency that underpins the whole model.
sections.threshold: Threshold pace and its anchoring heart rate are unchanged from the last test, which is now several weeks old — there's no new data to move the number in either direction. The trail block was run entirely at controlled, low HR, so it built durability rather than top-end aerobic power, and nothing since has tested threshold at all. The engine's demonstrated fitness is still there; it simply hasn't been probed recently, so treat the current figure as a standing estimate rather than a live reading.
sections.zones: There's no new run data to distribute across zones — the last logged sessions were almost entirely Z1, appropriate for the ultra-durability intent of that block, with only fleeting touches higher. The consequence of the ongoing pause is that the intensity distribution has effectively gone to zero: no easy volume, no grey-zone drift, and crucially no upper-zone work either. Whenever running resumes, the first sessions sitting cleanly back in easy Z1 at a normal HR is the signal to watch for.
sections.hr_comparison: Nothing new on the strength side — the most recent sessions are weeks old, and their HR shapes were unremarkable functional work sitting mostly low with brief elevated stretches, consistent with circuit-style sessions rather than heavy grinding. There's no fresh run HR to compare across sources today.
sections.calendar: The calendar tells the real story more bluntly than any single metric: a dense, front-loaded trail cluster followed by an unbroken run of empty structured days. The running and strength streaks both sit at zero. The consistency that this athlete's model depends on has a visible break in it now, and the length of that break is the thing that has changed most since the block ended — the reason no longer matters as much as the duration.
sections.personal_bests: No PBs are in reach while structured training is paused — the short-distance bests from last autumn reflect a speed-focused window that the recent trail block deliberately wasn't. When faster work returns, those 5K–Half marks are the relevant targets; the ultra durability just banked is a different currency entirely.

watch_items: Watch whether the first run finally appears and returns at a normal easy HR — this is now overdue as the single test of whether the block absorbed cleanly.
Watch whether the gap has now become a genuine unplanned layoff rather than earned recovery — duration is the deciding factor at this point.
Watch whether strength and running re-enter together or whether one leads — both have been dark for the same stretch.
Watch whether the high step floor is masking the absence of any structured stimulus in the athlete's own perception of load.
